publications.title: Adaptive Gaussian Splatting SLAM: Robust Dense Mapping With Probabilistic Optimization
publications.abstract: In this article, we present adaptive Gaussian splatting–simultaneous localization and mapping (AGS-SLAM), an red-green-blue-depth (RGB-D) Gaussian-based SLAM framework that injects uncertainty-aware and robust optimization into tracking, mapping, and loop closure. Unlike prior Gaussian SLAM pipelines that rely on deterministic updates and uniform residual weighting, AGS-SLAM renders per-pixel uncertainty from the Gaussian map and uses it to downweight unreliable regions during pose estimation, combined with a Tukey biweight objective whose scale is estimated automatically via median absolute deviation (MAD) for principled outlier suppression. On the mapping side, we introduce a multicue seeding strategy that fuses alpha holes, depth inconsistency, Sobel edges, and projected high-uncertainty Gaussians, and we optimize submaps with uncertainty-weighted photometric losses, uncertainty regularization, and scheduled pruning to stabilize geometry while preserving rendering fidelity. Finally, we add a lightweight submap-level loop-closure module using a training-free multicue hash descriptor, dynamic acceptance thresholds with contrastive margins and voting, followed by pose-graph optimization for global drift correction. Experiments on public RGB-D benchmarks and real-world sequences demonstrate that AGS-SLAM improves robustness and produces high-quality reconstructions under challenging sensing conditions.

publications.title: Supplementary materials for Toward Trustworthy Synthetic Media Forensics: A Review of Detection, Provenance, and Investigation Workflows
publications.abstract: Supplementary materials for the narrative integrative review "Toward Trustworthy Synthetic Media Forensics: A Review of Detection, Provenance, and Investigation Workflows" by Anfal Tariq, Muhammad Hamid, and Ali Sufyan, The Islamia University of Bahawalpur, Pakistan. S1 contains the 123-record cited-source ledger, logged discovery captures, and primary-source, DOI, date, and version verification records. The IEEE Xplore and Springer Nature Link updates are documented discovery searches; their captured records are distinguished from purposive author selection. The literature cutoff is October 9, 2026. Selected version, date, and numerical-result checks were completed on November 15, 2026. S2 contains descriptive source extraction, three supporting comparison tables, and source-reported numerical results with their training/test conditions and exact primary-table locators. S3 contains the proposed twenty-group reporting checklist, pinpoint source support, seven consistently named interface requirements, and future-evaluation mappings. S4 contains illustrative local exchange mappings, synthetic fixtures, deterministic outputs, and reproduction code. The archive also supplies the manuscript's six native LaTeX figure fragments and a SHA-256 file manifest. The checklist and omission scenarios remain proposed. No independent-coder audit, inter-rater agreement statistic, practitioner study, new detector evaluation, or real-consumer exchange benchmark is claimed. The related conceptual system design and unused human-audit forms are excluded from this release. Original review annotations and original illustrative code are offered under CC BY 4.0. Third-party metadata, specification captures, and vendored schema files retain their respective rights and licenses. Version 1.0.0; archive finalized November 15, 2026.

publications.title: Exploration Optimization for Dynamic Assortment Personalization under Linear Preferences
publications.abstract: We study dynamic assortment personalization, where an online retailer adaptively selects assortments based on customer attributes to learn preferences and maximize revenue. We assume that product utilities depend linearly on customer attributes through an unknown coefficient matrix, leading to an exploration–exploitation trade-off. We identify price-driven and linearity-driven exploration efficiencies, showing that not all products need to be offered to all customer profiles to recover optimal assortments. We establish an instance-dependent regret lower bound characterized by a linear program, which we call the Regret Lower Bound (RLB) problem. Because the RLB has a complex structure and depends non-trivially on unknown parameters, we introduce an alternative formulation, called the Exploration-Optimization problem, that yields an interpretable exploration structure and can be formulated as a tractable mixed-integer linear program. We develop learning policies that select efficient exploration sets by solving either problem and establish a regret upper bound for the Exploration-Optimization policy. Using data from a large Chilean retailer, we demonstrate that our policies substantially outperform Thompson sampling in terms of both regret and computational efficiency, while remaining scalable in practice.

publications.title: Capstone Sponsor Onboarding Ontology (CSO), version 0.2.1: OWL ontology, competency-question SPARQL queries and results
publications.abstract: Version 0.2.1 of the Capstone Sponsor Onboarding Ontology (CSO), an OWL 2 ontology for the onboarding of capstone design project sponsors: the interval between a sponsor's commitment and a student team's first productive week. It names actors, artifacts, activities, phases, decision gates, risks, adjustment constructs from organizational socialization theory, outcome measures, sponsor types and practices, and gives every practice an evidence level. Version 0.2.0 was frozen on 14 November 2026 as the codebook of a rapid systematic review of sponsor onboarding practices in capstone design; version 0.2.1 re-froze it on 15 November 2026, after the author's check of its coding calls and before any report was coded. The record also holds the ontology's 18 competency questions as SPARQL 1.1 queries, a Python script that runs them with rdflib, two synthetic test programs and the results (14 pass, 4 partial, 0 fail). Each evidence level carries a weight for a proposed readiness rubric, which has not been validated. License: CC BY 4.0.

publications.title: Communication-Aware Task Planning for Heterogeneous UUV Swarms in the Internet of Underwater Things
publications.abstract: The Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT) extends distributed sensing to marine environments, where unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) serve as mobile nodes for flexible underwater operations. This article investigates the heterogeneous UUV multitype task planning problem (HUMTTP) for a collaborative system comprising autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), underwater gliders (UGs), and bionic manta-ray underwater vehicles (BMUVs). Existing methods generally prioritize execution efficiency but often overlook platform heterogeneity and acoustic communication limitations. To address these issues, this article proposes a hierarchical task planning framework called REASOM-UCLNS. In the task allocation layer, the reward- and energy-aware self-organizing map (REASOM) algorithm incorporates a novel neuron-based reward estimation strategy into winner selection. By integrating the estimated platform-specific task rewards with current-aware energy evaluation, REASOM assesses the execution suitability of heterogeneous UUVs and facilitates the efficient allocation of multitype tasks. In the route planning layer, the underwater cooperative large neighborhood search (UCLNS) algorithm converts the generated task sets into feasible routes for individual UUVs. UCLNS develops two constraint-specific operators to restore route feasibility when communication connectivity or energy balance violations occur. By integrating targeted constraint handling into the destroy-repair process, UCLNS improves route quality while satisfying operational constraints. Numerical results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed framework. Finally, a lake experiment involving four heterogeneous AUVs further confirms its practical applicability.

publications.title: Reproducibility archive for: Losing tumor, gaining signal: the synaptic proteomic shift of recurrent glioblastoma reflects composition, not induction
publications.abstract: Complete reproducibility archive accompanying the manuscript Losing tumor, gaining signal: the synaptic proteomic shift of recurrent glioblastoma reflects composition, not induction (Research article, Acta Neuropathologica Communications). The archive regenerates every reported number from the supplied inputs: rna_state_technical/ - CARE and Wang paired malignant-nucleus RNA models, author-labeled state models, the 11-patient cell-average decomposition, linked CPTAC analyses and the technical-benchmark simulation outputs, including the a05 cell-class composition model and detection-requirement simulations. protein_and_flowcell/ - 96-patient/182-protein protein endpoint, two-covariate baseline-matched comparator, 26-plex bootstrap and leave-one-plex influence, and the 11-patient linked flowcell sensitivity. Each folder is self-contained (code/, inputs/, results/, source_metadata/). Python 3.11 (numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, pyreadr) and R 4.6 (limma, edgeR, TMM, fry); runtime versions and seeds are recorded in the scripts and in R_sessionInfo.txt. SHA256_manifest.json lists the digest and size of every file. Source data are public repositories (GSE274546, GSE174554, GSE138794, PDC000514, PDC000446, PRJNA1252365); third-party material remains subject to the terms of the original studies. No new sequencing data were generated.

publications.title: jsN: JavaScript Tools for Sample Size Calculation in Clinical Studies
publications.abstract: jsN is a JavaScript library and a collection of 40 web applications for sample size and power calculation in clinical and medical research. All calculations run in the web browser; no data are sent to a server. It covers continuous, binary and time-to-event outcomes, non-inferiority designs, mixed models for repeated measures, Simon's two-stage design and the randomized phase II selection design.

publications.title: Using Claude in Excel with the 360° MDL Toolkit: A practical guide to responsible AI assistance in multidimensional literature reviews
publications.abstract: A practical guide for researchers, doctoral students and supervisors who use Claude in Excel with the official 360MDL_Toolkit_v2026.xlsx of the 360° MDL — Multidimensional Literature Review Model, Version 2026 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23724393). Contents (20 pages). Set-up and requirements; a safe working protocol (clean master, dated copies, the Two-Key Rule: Claude proposes, the researcher verifies and confirms); persistent instructions to paste once; the 17 toolkit sheets mapped to the seven phases; 30 tested prompts, sheet by sheet, from the Review Canvas to the indices dashboard and the reporting checklist; a worked example; checks against invented references and overwritten formulas; and ready-to-use AI-use disclosure text for a thesis or paper. Part of the 360° MDL ecosystem. Methodology doi:10.5281/zenodo.23724393 · Index Calculator doi:10.5281/zenodo.24033376 · Navigator agent doi:10.5281/zenodo.24041175 · Student Handbook doi:10.5281/zenodo.24241346 · PhD Playbook doi:10.5281/zenodo.23777000 · site https://mlytras.github.io/360mdl/. publications.title: Source records, endpoint data and reproducible figures for From Grasp Acquisition to Reliable Task Completion
publications.abstract: Review-authored supplementary materials for a critical review of language-conditioned and vision-language-action manipulation. The deposit contains the preserved S1-S6 evidence snapshot, the targeted benchmark update through 15 November 2026, 18 source-defined endpoint observations, editable tables, eight figure designs, reproducible plotting and TikZ code, a 172-source literature-and-photograph catalogue and a citation crosswalk. All 170 original bibliographic records remain in the integrated article; two additional records credit genuine robot photographs. The repository is cited separately in the final manuscript. The source snapshot covers a non-exhaustive critical synthesis and is not a meta-analysis. Source-specific denominators, interventions, publication versions and unresolved endpoint qualifications remain explicit. Experimental video frames from Johannsmeier et al. (2025) and Nazari et al. (2025) are attributed under CC BY 4.0. This record contains review-derived material, not new robot experiments, original paper PDFs, or redistributed Web of Science abstracts. No specific funding was received.
